text:
Ajay (Sales): Heads-up — Nimbus (enterprise) is talking a 12‑month commit. POC next Tue. They said peak ~4k RPS, baseline ~800 RPS, avg ~60 tokens/request, conversational with context up to 1k tokens. Need sizing for reserved GPUs, autoscale policy, and pricing delta. Any immediate blockers? @Maya @Devin

Maya (Solutions): Quick q — is 4k RPS sustained or bursty? what's the 95th/99th tail? streaming enabled? any KV/prefix reuse in flows?

Ajay (Sales): They said bursts ~10s every ~10 minutes, sustained baseline ~800, p95 ~2k, p99 ~3.3k. Streaming enabled. Sessions have high prefix reuse (~70%).

Devin (Platform Eng): Ok. For that profile main levers are: KV cache seeding, batching window (~20ms), and prewarm slots. Rough capacity estimate: quantized Llama‑2‑70B on A100‑80GB ~250–350 effective p95 RPS per GPU with batching + KV reuse; H100 roughly 1.5–2x that. Important: numbers vary a lot with p95 SLO and streaming.

Alex (SRE): Also callout: p95 latency target will change effective throughput. What SLO are they expecting?

Ajay (Sales): They want p95 <= 350ms across commit. We can flex a bit (negotiate to 400ms) if needed. Also security questionnaire expects VPC, SOC2 controls — they flagged that but it's standard.

Maya (Solutions): Actionable suggestion: Reserved fleet = 10 H100 (or ~14 A100‑80GB) running a quantized int8 model. Autoscale configured to use burst credits to expand to 20 GPUs during spikes. Prewarm: seed KV cache and keep ~50 prewarm slots per GPU. Use a hosted/model fallback route (smaller quantized model) for extreme spikes. I'll draft config + runbook.

Devin (Platform Eng): Proposed config snippet (for POC):
```yaml
autoscale:
  min_gpus: 10
  max_gpus: 20
  scale_up_threshold_rps: 1800   # cluster-wide RPS to trigger scale up
  scale_down_threshold_rps: 1200
  scale_up_cooldown_s: 45
  scale_down_cooldown_s: 300
prewarm:
  slots_per_gpu: 50
  kv_prefill: true
  kv_prefill_window_s: 600
model:
  quantization: "int8"
  fallback_model: "llama-2-13b-quant"
```
Also sample command to seed KV from their exported sessions:
```
curl -X POST https://internal-prefill/api/v1/prefill \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $PREFILL_TOKEN' \
  -d '{"session_samples_s3":"s3://nimbus-poc/samples.jsonl"}'
```

Maya (Solutions): Nice. Two other notes: 1) region fallback — route to another region if AZ exhausted; 2) model fallback for cost-savings during long tails. Legal will want reserved terms and a run rate cap.

Ajay (Sales): Can we get a cost ballpark for 10 H100 reserved vs 14 A100? Also what's cold-start risk if idle >30m?

Devin (Platform Eng): Ballpark numbers (region dependent): reserved 10 H100 ≈ $120k–180k/mo; 14 A100 ≈ similar order but slightly cheaper. I'll get exact quotes from infra procurement. Cold-start: without prewarm and KV seed cold-start p95 can be 1.2–1.8s; with prewarm + KV seed we should be <400ms for most requests.

Alex (SRE): Confirming: prewarm + KV seed+ short batching window will eliminate most spike latency. We should also configure circuit-breaker fallback to the hosted small model for extreme outliers to avoid queue buildup.

Maya (Solutions): I'll prepare: POC runbook, prewarm script, autoscale config, and answers for the security questionnaire.

Devin (Platform Eng): I'll run internal perf runs against their traffic sample and post measured p95/p99 and tokens/s per GPU by EOD tomorrow.

Ajay (Sales): I'll ask the customer for sanitized traffic traces and confirm SLO flexibility. Owners: Maya — runbook + sec answers; Devin — perf numbers + final config; Ajay — customer samples + legal handoff.

Ajay (Sales): Thanks all — will update once I have traces. :thumbsup:
